activities.title: Lane Entry Game
activities.constraint: Players act based on visible cues created by the constraint. Central pressure. Increase defensive pressure in central areas. Use wide areas. Provide scoring or positional advantage in wide areas. Penetrate into final third. Reward advancement into attacking areas through successful progression.
activities.intent: Keep the ball as a team and look for the moment to move it forward into the far end.
activities.setup: Two teams play in the marked area. Each team attacks the end the coach points. Mark an attacking zone across the far third of the pitch at each end. Teams play 6v6. Play in a 40 x 30 m (44 x 33 yd) area.
scaffolding: Watch how players read where the space is before they receive.
Coach observation: focus on the live decisions — how players read pressure, space, and support, and how they adapt when the picture changes.
Session focus: Maintain possession with forward intent.
Possession kept under live pressure is scored when retention itself is the contest.
Watch whether possession is maintained or secured under live opponent pressure; losing the ball once the space closes hands the advantage to the opponent.
extensions: Two teams compete in the same direction, with one team trying to keep and progress possession toward the target while the other applies pressure and tries to regain to attack back. Even numbers.
equipmentNeeded: Cones to mark the area and its zones
rules: Start with the ball at one end.
Play continues until the coach stops it.
Keep the ball and work it forward under pressure. Force it or lose it and the other team attacks straight away. Play does not stop.
activities.scoringSystem: Earn a point when a player dribbles into the attacking zone, or receives the ball there and controls it, and your team keeps the ball. Passing it around without moving forward never scores. Points are worth most through the middle, then wide, then deep.
activities.winCondition: The team with more points when time is up wins.

primaryScoring.scoringRule: Earn a point when a player dribbles into the attacking zone, or receives the ball there and controls it, and your team keeps the ball. Passing it around without moving forward never scores.
primaryScoring.setupRequirement: Mark an attacking zone across the far third of the pitch at each end.
primaryScoring.qualifyingCondition: Purposeful advancement from the attack's starting condition rather than possession alone: reaching a more advanced representative area while maintaining attacking possession.
